title: Thank You For Leading — 12 Legendary Leaders on the Importance of Gratitude
author: The Business Leader Daily
summary: The Business Leader Daily frames gratitude as an operational leadership imperative rather than a soft nicety, opening with a pointed paradox: withholding appreciation is not hard-nosed pragmatism but a form of negligence that silently erodes the engagement, motivation, and commitment leaders most depend on. The bulk of the piece is a curated anthology of twelve short quotations from well-known figures—Charles M. Schwab, Jack Canfield, Adrian Gostick and Chester Elton, Oprah Winfrey, Ralph Nader, Bill Bradley, John C. Maxwell, Zig Ziglar, Danita Bye, Roy T. Bennett, Tony Robbins, and Fred De Witt Van Amburgh—assembled around the theme that appreciation develops people and fuels performance. A cited research note claims a “staggering gratitude deficit in the work world,” with people less likely to express gratitude at work than anyplace else. The editorial through-line is that gratitude is a renewable, cost-free resource leaders under-deploy, and the collection functions as a Thanksgiving-timed reminder to make thanking one’s team a deliberate habit. Its value is as a compact, quotable reference on the leadership case for appreciation.
points: The framing reframes appreciation as risk management: withholding thanks is described not as tough pragmatism but as a form of negligence that erodes engagement and commitment—the very things leaders depend on.

The piece surfaces a research claim of a “staggering gratitude deficit in the work world” (per Gostick and Elton), with people reportedly less likely to express gratitude at work than anyplace else—locating the workplace as the setting most starved of it.
Schwab’s maxim anchors the collection’s thesis that appreciation is developmental: the way to develop the best in a person is by appreciation and encouragement.
Van Amburgh’s line captures the resource logic—gratitude as “a currency that we can mint for ourselves, and spend without fear of bankruptcy”—positioning appreciation as renewable and cost-free.
As a curated digest with editorial framing rather than a bare link-list, the collection earns its own archive slot and works as a quick reference for the leadership case for appreciation.
quotes: It’s actually a form of negligence that silently erodes the very thing we need most, people who are engaged, motivated, and committed to our shared mission.
The way to develop the best that is in a person is by appreciation and encouragement.
Gratitude is the single most important ingredient to living a successful and fulfilled life.
Our research and that of others shows that there is a staggering gratitude deficit in the work world.
Gratitude is a currency that we can mint for ourselves, and spend without fear of bankruptcy.
Among the things you can give and still keep are your word, a smile, and a grateful heart.
